sources.title: How to Visit Liuhe Pagoda – China Travel Tips
sources.content:
Liuhe Pagoda: Complete Visitor Information

Historical Background
The original pagoda was constructed in 970 AD to regulate the tidal bore of Qiantang River and serve as a lighthouse. It was destroyed during warfare in 1121. The current structure features a 7-storey inner stone pagoda and 13-storey outer wooden pagoda. The inner stone portion dates to the Southern Song Dynasty (1127–1279), while the outer wooden structure was added during the Qing Dynasty (1368–1644). The octagonal structure stands approximately 60 meters tall.

Location & Access
The pagoda is situated on Yuelun Hill, about 6.5 kilometers south of downtown Hangzhou along the northern bank of Qiantang River.

Transportation Options:
- Taxi: Approximately 25 RMB
- Public buses: Lines Y5, K808, K599, and 504 (2-3 yuan fare)
- Bicycle: Docking station available below Yuelun Hill

Admission & Hours
- Entrance fee: 20 RMB
- Pagoda climbing fee: Additional 10 RMB
- Closing time: 5:30 PM
- Visitor capacity: Limited to 200 people inside the pagoda simultaneously

Main Attractions

Pagoda Climbing: Visitors ascend wooden spiral staircases through seven floors to reach the summit, offering panoramic views of Qiantang River and surrounding landscape.

Liuhe Stele Pavilion: Features the historic Liuhe Bell, struck traditionally to ward off tidal forces and seek blessings.

Garden Areas: Goldfish Garden with pond, Imitation Ancient Pagoda Garden showcasing various dynasties' architectural styles.

Kaihua Temple Area: Now operates as a teahouse and exhibition space documenting the pagoda's history.

Facilities
Clean, well-equipped restroom facilities are available at the main entrance.

sources.title: Liuhe Pagoda | Travel Guide of Six Harmonies Pagoda, Hangzhou
sources.content:
Six Harmonies Pagoda (Liuhe Pagoda) - Hangzhou

Overview
Liuhe Pagoda or Six Harmonies Pagoda is a famous tower in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. It is also a perfect place to enjoy the panorama view of Qiantang River.

The pagoda is named after the Buddhist concept of "six harmonies of respect" (六和敬). Originally built in 970 CE during the Song Dynasty's Kaibao period, on the site of what was formerly the South Orchard of Wu Yue King Qian Hongzao, it was constructed to suppress the tides of the Qiantang River.

The Six Harmonies Pagoda opens daily from 6:30 in the morning to 5:30 in the evening, with the main ticket costing 20 yuan per person and an extra 10 yuan to climb to the top.

You can explore the pagoda and gardens in about 1.5 to 2 hours, or plan for 3 hours if you want to relax, take photos, or visit nearby spots.

The best view of the Qiantang River comes from the seventh floor. Each level of the pagoda is marked with intricate carvings and elaborate designs, with each ceiling of the 7 floors having paintings of flowers, animals, humans, and birds, and the eaves wearing a total of 104 iron bells.

September is best for mild weather and the Qiantang River tidal bore; spring (March–April) is good for nearby peony blooms.

There is a control over the number of visitors inside the pagoda, which is limited to 200 people. If at a time 200 visitors are climbing the pagoda, you have to wait.

The stairs are described as very steep, presenting a physical challenge but rewarding climbers with panoramic views of the Qiantang River. Children and seniors are not recommended to make the ascent.

For travel inquiries: Phone +86-28-85227275, Email info@chinadiscovery.com

sources.title: Six Harmonies Pagoda, Liuhe Pagoda, Hangzhou
sources.content:
Six Harmonies Pagoda, Liuhe Pagoda, Hangzhou

The pagoda is located on Yuelun Hill, Zhijiang Road, Xihu District, Hangzhou City.

Opening Hours: Seasonal hours of 7:00 to 17:30 (April – October) and 7:00 to 16:55 (November – March).

Admission Fees: 20 RMB for adults, 10 RMB for students/seniors, free for children under 1.2m and seniors over 70. An additional CNY 10/person is required for pagoda climbing.

Public Transportation: Take bus 4, 287, 318, 334 or 354 to Liuhe Ta (Six Harmonies Pagoda) Station, or take bus 190, 202, 280, 308, 595a, 595b or 597, and get off at Zhijianglu Liuheta Station.

A taxi/rideshare from West Lake is approximately a 20-minute ride (approx. 30–40 RMB).

Duration: You can explore the pagoda and gardens in about 1.5 to 2 hours, or plan for 3 hours if you want to relax, take photos, or visit nearby spots.

Footwear: The spiral staircase is steep and narrow, so comfortable shoes are recommended.

Best time for views: The best view of the Qiantang River comes from the seventh floor.

sources.title: Hangzhou attractions – Six Harmonies Pagoda
sources.content:
Hangzhou attractions – Six Harmonies Pagoda

The Six Harmonies Pagoda overlooks the Qiantang River and is a towering structure that is more than just a remarkable feat of ancient engineering; it is a storied landmark weaving together tales of dynastic histories and Buddhist symbolism.

The experience of viewing the Six Harmonies Pagoda can vary significantly depending on the time of day and the season, with certain times offering more spectacular views than others for photographers and sightseers alike.

As visitors ascend the spiral staircase, they encounter a series of windows on each floor, offering varying perspectives of the river and the city. There are many wooden windows at Six Harmonies Pagoda which are very popular on the internet, with people using them to take photos.

Each level of the pagoda is marked with intricate carvings and elaborate designs, with each ceiling of the 7 floors having paintings of flowers, animals, humans, and birds, and the eaves wearing a total of 104 iron bells.

If you visit during a busy season, try to arrive early, which helps you avoid crowds and gives you more time to explore. Plan for 1.5–2 hours for time to climb the pagoda and explore the grounds.

sources.title: Liuhe Pagoda (Six Harmonies Pagoda) in Hangzhou
sources.content:
Liuhe Pagoda (Six Harmonies Pagoda) in Hangzhou

Liuhe Pagoda, first built in 970 AD, is one of the three most famous ancient towers in Hangzhou. The pagoda opens from 7:00 AM–5:30 PM.

Entrance fees: 20 RMB for adults and an additional 10 RMB for ascending the pagoda.

Liuhe Pagoda stands on Yuelun Hill in the south of downtown Hangzhou and northern bank of Qiantang River, around 6.5km from the city center.

Transportation options include: A pleasant taxi ride to Liuhe Pagoda costs about RMB 25. Public buses of Line Y5, K808, K599 and 504 at the bus fare of 2 or 3 yuan. Riding a bike is an option, with a big docking station below the Yuelun Hill.

The pagoda is now part of Liuhe Pagoda Scenic Area, which is composed of 4 major areas – Liuhe Pagoda Area, Kaihua Temple Area, Liuhe Stele Pavilion and Liuhe Pagoda Garden Area.

sources.title: 六和塔_百度百科
sources.content:
六和塔完整信息汇总

基本信息
中文名：六和塔
外文名：Liuhe Pagoda（Six Harmonies Pagoda）
地理位置：浙江省杭州市西湖区之江路16号
占地面积：890平方米（约1.3亩）
保护级别：第一批国家重点文物保护单位
建筑年代：南宋

历史沿革
北宋开宝三年（970年），吴越王钱弘俶听从延寿、赞宁两禅师建议，在此建九级高塔以镇江潮，取佛教六种规约命塔为六和塔。宣和三年（1121年），六和塔因兵火被毁。南宋绍兴二十二年（1152年），改六和寺为开化寺。绍兴二十六年（1156年），智昙禅师重修，改九层塔为七层塔。隆兴元年（1163年），重建六和塔，共七层。明嘉靖十二年（1533年），倭寇入侵杭州，塔遭破坏；万历年间大规模修缮。清雍正十三年（1735年），李卫再作大规模整修，历时两年建成。清乾隆十六年（1751年），皇帝南巡来杭登塔游览，七层各题匾额，并题诗联。清咸丰十一年（1861年），塔遭兵燹，外廓木廊损坏严重。清光绪二十五年（1899年）再作大规模修缮，重建十三层木檐廊。光绪二十六年（1900年），在塔外木构檐廊十三层。外二层为内一层，六层封闭，七层与塔外相通，形成明七暗三的独特构造。

建筑特点
塔高59.89米，塔身为砖砌，外檐为木结构，平面呈八角形。外檐13层，7层与塔身相通，6层封闭，形成7明6暗的格局。塔外各层檐角挂有104只铁铃。塔身仿木结构形式砌筑，塔内有阶梯可盘旋而上，到达顶层。塔身每层有外墙、回廊、内墙和方形塔心小室四部分。每层方形中心塔室，用斗拱承托藻井。

门道两侧有壁龛，龛下设须弥座，塔室外墙回廊间也设壁龛和须弥座。须弥座的束腰部分，雕刻各式题材，花卉有石榴、荷花、宝相、牡丹等；飞禽有凤凰、孔雀、鹦鹉等；走兽有狮子、麒麟等。还有飞仙、迦陵嫔伽与乐伎等精美雕刻。

壁龛嵌有南宋《四十二章经》石刻。廊间南门立南宋尚书省牒碑。北面有明朝线刻真武画像碑。3层有《金刚般若波罗密经》刻石嵌于壁间。

文物遗存
六和塔内文物有明石刻镇海神像、南宋'救赐开化之寺'石碑以及清乾隆皇帝游塔时手书的六和塔塔碑。乾隆御碑高4.35米，宽1.5米。六和塔内铸像是南宋开化寺主持智昙大师铜像。六和塔内铜钟高0.95米，重2.3吨。

研究价值
六和塔庄严而又雄伟，远望有拔地参天之势，为杭州古城最重要的宋代建筑，标志南宋时期的建筑科技与艺术水准。

典故传说
据《水浒传》记载：梁山泊的英雄花和尚鲁智深圆寂于此。景阳冈打虎英雄武松后来也老死于此。故塔内还留有鲁智深和武松的画像。

历代诗词
郭沫若曾登上六和塔赋诗：'登上六和最上层，钱塘江畔岭纵横。千年胜迹垂千古，百代游人尽百生。'
陈毅留下'置身如在画屏中，景色钱塘傲大空'的诗句。
乾隆帝为六和塔每层题字：初地坚固、二谛俱融、三明净域、四天宝纲、五云覆盖、六鳖负载、七宝庄严。

开放时间与门票
开放时间：夏令时间07:00-17:30，冬令时间07:00-16:55
门票价格：30.00元（含登塔）

交通指南
地铁：乘坐杭州地铁4号线至水澄桥站下车，从B口出站。
公交：六和塔站4、4B、314、318；之江路六和塔站39、500、8202

sources.title: Liuhe Pagoda - Wikipedia
sources.content:
Liuhe Pagoda (Six Harmonies Pagoda) is a multi-storied Chinese pagoda in southern Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, China. It is located at the foot of Yuelun Hill, facing the Qiantang River. It was originally constructed in 970 CE and has been destroyed and rebuilt several times.

The name 'Liuhe' means 'six harmonies' and refers to the six Buddhist doctrines of harmony: body, speech, mind, morality, views, and livelihood. The pagoda was first built by the monks of the Kaihua Temple during the Northern Song dynasty to calm the tidal bore of the Qiantang River.

The current structure dates from the Southern Song dynasty (1165), with the exterior wooden structure added during the Qing dynasty (1900). The pagoda has a brick inner structure of seven stories and an exterior wooden structure of thirteen stories, creating the illusion of thirteen floors from the outside. It stands approximately 60 meters (200 feet) tall with an octagonal plan.

The pagoda was designated as a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level in 1961.

sources.title: 杭州六和塔旅游攻略（开放时间+门票+地址交通）
sources.content:
杭州六和塔旅游攻略

六和塔位于西湖之南，钱塘江畔月轮山上。北宋开宝三年（公元970年），当时杭州为吴越国国都，国王为镇住钱塘江潮水派僧人智元禅师建造了六和塔。如今的六和塔塔身重建于南宋。

开放时间与门票
公园门票：20元，登塔另收10元。开放时间：06:30-17:30(全年开放)

门票优惠政策
70周岁及以上老人、现役军人、残疾人、离休干部、消防救援、在职公安民警、残疾军人、烈士遗属、因公牺牲军人遗属、病故军人遗属、离退休军官、30年以上教龄的教师凭有效证件免费参观。对6周岁（不含）以上—18周岁（含）未成年、全日制大学本科及以下学历在读学生实行半价优惠。

购票方式
预约通道：关注'西湖旅游'微信公众号，点击菜单栏-景区门票即可进入购票页面。

交通方式
乘坐4路、318路等多路公交车在'六和塔'公交站下车步行即可抵达。

游玩特色
站在六和塔上，远眺钱塘江，江水悠悠东去，倒是很有一幅站在古代四大名楼上望水怀古的情调。
